title: Israeli Forces Detain 12 Palestinians in Overnight West Bank Raids; Settlers Burn Two Vehicles in Beita
detail: Overnight into Wednesday, September 2, 2026, Israeli forces conducted raids across multiple West Bank towns, detaining 12 Palestinians. In Balata refugee camp east of Nablus, forces detained three Palestinians; in the al-Jawza neighborhood of Nablus' Old City, soldiers raided a metal workshop, seized equipment, and detained its owner along with his two sons after also raiding their home. In al-Rashaydeh village east of Bethlehem, forces raided several homes and detained and questioned four Palestinians, while in the town of Aqaba, north of Tubas, two young men were detained after their homes were raided. Separately, Israeli settlers set fire to two Palestinian vehicles parked in front of residents' homes in the eastern part of Beita, a town south of Nablus, early Wednesday morning. According to the Wall and Settlement Resistance Commission, settlers carried out 628 attacks across the West Bank in the preceding month alone, with Ramallah and al-Bireh (157 incidents) and Nablus (137) the hardest-hit governorates.

media.caption: Burned vehicles in the town of Beita, south of Nablus, after a settler arson attack, September 2, 2026

confidenceReason: Detention count and locations corroborated across WAFA (Palestinian Authority's official news agency), Anadolu Agency's wire report via the Express Tribune, and Middle East Monitor; IDF has not disputed that raids occurred.

title: Israeli Forces Tear-Gas Worshippers Inside Madama Mosque; Settlers Attempt to Burn Bazariya Mosque
detail: On Tuesday, September 1 into Wednesday, September 2, 2026, Israeli forces fired tear gas canisters into a mosque in the village of Madama, south of Nablus, during evening prayers, causing worshippers — including elderly attendees — to suffocate and flee, according to footage verified by Al Jazeera. Hours earlier, Israeli settlers attempted to set fire to the Nur al-Din Zanki Mosque in the nearby village of Bazariya (Bizzariya), roughly 13km northwest of Nablus, pouring flammable liquid onto the ground floor and igniting it; resident Majed Nasr said locals 'managed to contain the blaze' before it reached the upper building, and Hebrew-language graffiti was sprayed on the exterior walls. The Palestinian Ministry of Religious Affairs said at least 13 mosques have been 'violated' by Israeli forces or settlers since the start of 2026, with attacks on religious sites roughly tripling since the Gaza war began in October 2023.

media.caption: Palestinians inspect the Nur al-Din Zanki Mosque in Bazariya after a settler arson attempt, September 1-2, 2026

confidenceReason: Both incidents corroborated by Al Jazeera's own footage verification, the Palestinian Ministry of Religious Affairs, and an on-the-record resident quote; Israeli authorities have not disputed the tear-gassing or arson attempt.
